newsitem.title: GERMANY: FAG sees growing Frankfurt airport handling competition.
newsitem.headline: FAG sees growing Frankfurt airport handling competition.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said it would compete strongly for airline clients in a liberalised cargo handling market at Frankfurt airport.
FAG airfreight director Frank Fischer said the authority aimed to hit back at rival handling firms which offered lower rates.
Fischer told Reuters in an interview: "We have seen that the pedestal on which we sat is not there any more. We are in full competition."
"Price is not always everything but for some airlines it is decisive," he added.
FAG currently handles the air cargo of 70 of the 100 or so airlines operating at Frankfurt airport and will take over cargo handling for Delta Air Lines from June.
Fischer added: "We are negotiating with Air New Zealand, Asiana Airlines and several others. The loss of several airlines has been evened out."
The leading rival to FAG is Luftfracht-Umschlag GmbH (LUG) which had expanded into export cargo handling and will open a Cargo City South freight complex in August, industry sources noted.
LUG has recently won deals with Korean Air Lines, Air India and Lan Chile to take over export and import handling from May, they said.
Lufthansa Cargo and several smaller airlines do their own cargo handling while another rival is Wisskirchen Transporte GmbH which is building a Cargo City South freight centre.
Fischer said he expected FAG to handle up to 330,000 tonnes of cargo this year, a 10 percent rise on 1996 generated through market growth and acquisitions.
The total freight volume handled at Frankfurt airport last year was 1.36 million tonnes, a figure expected to double to 2.7 million tonnes in 2010.
Fischer added: "We will continue to look for new business. We will expand our range of services, both in forwarding and in handling. We want to be an all-rounder supplier."
